premises.text: Status and project communications containing valuable business information remain inaccessible company-wide when sent as private email
premises.evidence_span: the rest of the company can't access them. As a result, decisions are less informed, work is duplicated

premises.text: A simple manager setup of recipients, schedule, and report template collects consistent status reports without chasing writers
premises.evidence_span: She enters the email addresses for her employees. She chooses a schedule, in this case, Friday afternoon, and selects a template

premises.text: Central recipient lists and project follow make shared reports reachable like a social follow graph rather than copy-paste email blasts
premises.evidence_span: each of these people can follow a project just as easily as they can follow someone on Twitter

premises.text: Aggregated status reports let employees search for internal expertise, client relationships, and location that would otherwise stay in other inboxes
premises.evidence_span: her company has that information, but she can't access it because it's stuck in someone else's inbox

value.text: Each person understands where their work fits in the company puzzle so people and resources align
value.evidence_span: each person understanding the entire puzzle and where their pieces fit in

causal_links.evidence_span: companies lose money because of this
making status reports more accessible, by making them more consistent
more powerful to align people and resources across an organization

notes: Independent coding: folded consistency/timeliness/reminders into the collection setup premise rather than splitting. Business-graph framing treated as the search/access mechanism in P4, not a separate premise (v1.3.2 clarification 4/5). Truncated closing. Singleton D1 and D3 retained as separately revisable problem and discovery modules.
